Will/Won't in the If-Clause
You usually use will/won't with a conditional clause when you want to talk about possibility in the present or future. There are some exceptions to this rule:
1. If you will ... = if you insist on ...
When you use will it means the same as the verb insist on. When you say this kind of structure, you place a lot of word stress on will:
If you will run twenty kilometers a day, it's not surprising your feet hurt. =
If you insist on running so much, it's not surprising you have sore feet.
2. If you won't ... = if you refuse to ...
Won't (will not) means that you refuse to do something. When you use won't in a sentence it is usually stressed.
If he won't come camping with the group, we will get him to come one way or another.
If he refuses to come camping with the group, there's nothing we can do to make him.
Some leaders believe that if the refugees will make the dangerous voyage, then they will have to face the possible consequences.

However, if thousands of exhausted migrants won't wait in weeks-long waiting lines, then the German government will have a major problem on their hands.
Causative Get and Have

You use a causative verb when you want to talk about an action that was done by another person for you or someone. This means that the subject of the sentence was what caused the action to occur, but they didn't do it themselves.
You use the causative verbs get/have when you want to make it clear that it was the subject that paid, asked, or persuaded the other person to do the action.
For example:
Have your kids clean up their room.
In this sentence you ask or persuade your kids to clean their room.
The structure of the causative is:

have + object + verb
Have someone remind everyone.
or
Subject + get + object + Infinitive
I got Sandra to remind everyone.

images.text: With the decimation of cities in Syria, refugees have been flooding into Europe in search of a new life. They had their lives torn apart and their livelihoods ripped away from them by political instability and foreign invasion. Knowing that millions of people were searching for assistance, European leaders quickly scrambled to create policies and got additional border patrol officials prepared to manage the desperate people. Some leaders believe that if the refugees will make the dangerous voyage, then they will have to face the possible consequences.

Others have stated that if the refugees won't use the correct way of applying for residency, they will have few options. When Germany publicly stated that they would overlook United Nations protocol so that Syrian migrants could apply for asylum despite their means of arrival, many expected a sea of people. Indeed, hopeful families fled their country ripped apart from social strife and political unrest.

Now, Germany is struggling to deal with the thousands of refugees crossing their borders. Towns and cities cannot easily accommodate all the refugees.  Authorities have found it difficult to provide all the services and accommodation necessary to assist the refugees on such short notice. Some refugees got their paperwork organized and returned quickly. However, if thousands of exhausted migrants won't wait in weeks-long waiting lines, then the German government will have a major problem on their hands.  Now, that winter is approaching, this logistical nightmare will become dire.
What should I include in my paragraph?
